findings.title: DisplayQrCode "Continue" button is type="submit" inside outer Form, fires handleEnable API call
findings.body: The "Continue" button on the QR code step is rendered as type="submit" and lives inside the outer <Form handleSubmit={handleEnable}> (Form opens at line 209). Clicking it both runs the onClick (which advances to EnterTotpCode) AND submits the form, invoking handleEnable which immediately calls TwoFactorAuthAPI.enable() with whatever totpCode is currently in the form (empty or stale from a previous attempt). The result is a wasted API round-trip and an error toast like "code is incorrect" being briefly shown to the user before the step transitions. The button should be type="button" since its only intent is to advance the wizard step.

findings.title: ConfirmPassword "Continue" button is type="submit" inside outer Form, fires two API calls
findings.body: The ConfirmPassword Continue button is type="submit" and is placed inside the outer <Form handleSubmit={handleEnable}> (Form opens at line 209, the button is at line 233-240). Clicking it both runs the onClick handleSetup (which posts to /api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup) and submits the outer form which calls handleEnable, which posts to /api/auth/two-factor/totp/enable. Because totpCode is empty at this point, the second call always fails and sets an error message in state, even on a successful setup. The button should be type="button" (or moved outside the outer Form) so that only handleSetup runs.

findings.title: Race condition allows backup code to be reused under concurrent requests
findings.body: After a backup code is matched (line 144), the code nulls the used slot in memory and then awaits a prisma.user.update to persist (lines 148-156). Two concurrent login requests that submit the same backup code will both pass the indexOf check against the same in-memory array before either write hits the DB, and both will be authenticated. The second write then overwrites the first with the same nulled array, so the code remains "consumed" but two sessions are created. Mitigation: do the read/compare/null/write atomically (e.g. via prisma.$transaction with a conditional update that only matches if the code is still present), or perform a single UPDATE that removes the specific code rather than rewriting the whole array.

findings.title: No rate limiting on 2FA disable endpoint, enabling brute-force of TOTP/backup code
findings.body: The disable handler accepts a TOTP code (6 digits, ~20 bits of entropy) or a backup code (10 hex chars, 40 bits) and attempts verification on every request. Unlike the next-auth credentials authorize (which calls checkRateLimitAndThrowError), this endpoint performs no rate limiting, no lockout, and no failed-attempt counter. A user who is still logged in (or an attacker with a stolen session cookie) can submit unlimited guesses. TOTP is especially vulnerable: 10^6 / 30s is small enough that a targeted attacker can reliably find the current code. Add checkRateLimitAndThrowError (or equivalent) keyed on the user id before running code verification.

findings.title: Object URL for backup codes download is never revoked on unmount
findings.body: A new object URL is created (line 99) and the previous one is revoked only when another URL is created (line 98). When the modal is closed or the component unmounts, the last backupCodesUrl is never revoked, leaking the underlying Blob for the lifetime of the page. Add a cleanup useEffect that calls URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl) on unmount, and also revoke it in resetState() / when the user navigates away from DisplayBackupCodes.

findings.title: Returns 200 success without authenticating when 2FA is not enabled, leaking 2FA status
findings.body: When user.twoFactorEnabled is false, the endpoint short-circuits with `return res.json({ message: "Two factor disabled" })` (line 37) without ever calling verifyPassword or checking the supplied code. Any caller who knows a valid session can use this to probe whether a given account has 2FA enabled: the response body and status differ from the "needs 2FA / needs password" branches. Either require the same authentication as the 2FA-enabled path before returning, or return a uniform response regardless of 2FA status.

findings.title: Backup code authentication path is not exercised by any test
findings.body: The e2e file has a TODO at line 12 ("add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup") and only verifies UI affordances (download/copy/close). The new security-critical paths added in this PR — backup-code login via next-auth-options.ts, backup-code disable via totp/disable.ts, single-use enforcement of backup codes, and the IncorrectBackupCode / MissingBackupCodes ErrorCode mappings in login.tsx — are not covered. Without these tests, regressions in single-use enforcement, race-condition fixes, or error mapping will go undetected. The author also explicitly ticked the checklist item "I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works".

findings.title: formatBackupCode referenced before declaration; download Blob built on first render
findings.body: handleSetup (line 77) references formatBackupCode (line 163) inside its body. Because formatBackupCode is a const arrow function declared after handleSetup, this works only via closure hoisting at call time — easy to break by future refactors and confusing to read. More importantly, the Blob on line 95 is built using formatBackupCode but the downloaded file content can drift from what is shown on screen if the formatter changes between setup and download (e.g. different dash placement). Define formatBackupCode before handleSetup (module scope or above the component) so both the display grid (line 204) and the Blob/copy operations (lines 95, 278) use the same definition.
